Settings for model parameters when publishing a web tool.

This text will appear as the parameter name in the web tool interface. The label should be short, descriptive of the purpose of the parameter, and written in plain language.

This text will appear as the parameter's pop-up help and will provide information to the web tool user about how to populate the tool parameter. Include a description of what the parameter does, how different values impact the tool results, the supported inputs, and the default values as necessary.

The supported data type for the parameter. This value is determined by the variable data type and cannot be changed.

Specifies whether the parameter is an input or output. This value is determined by the tool parameter and cannot be changed.

Specifies whether the parameter has a default value. When turned on, the parameter will use a default value based on the variable value. When turned off, the parameter will be empty by default. A default value can be used to guide the user's inputs or make the web tool easier to run because the user does not need to update the parameter manually.

Default values should not be used for parameters you may want to leave empty (for example, an optional input dataset).

The default value for the parameter. To change the default value, update the value of the variable in the model diagram. The default value should be a value that will give an accurate or preferred result in most cases.

Specifies whether the parameter is required to run the web tool. If the model parameter is connected to one or more required tool parameters, this value will be turned on and will not be editable. If all connected tool parameters are optional, the model parameter can be turned on to make the parameter required or turned off to make the parameter optional. Making a parameter required will force the user to provide an input before the web tool can be run.

Specifies whether the tool parameter inputs will have restrictions. Filter options depend on the parameter type as follows:

  • String—Select which unique values are available.
  • Feature layer—Select which feature types are available.
  • Integer—Specify a minimum and maximum value.
  • Double—Specify a minimum and maximum value.
